quests.instruction: A poster is due in 5 days. Which shows a plan that breaks the job into steps?
quests.correctAnswer: Research Monday, draw Tuesday, write Wednesday 📅
options: Wait until an idea comes to you first 🤷
Do everything on the night before it is due 🌙
Research Monday, draw Tuesday, write Wednesday 📅
quests.explanation: Splitting a big task into smaller steps makes it feel manageable.
quests.funFact: Builders and engineers split big projects into smaller steps called milestones.

quests.instruction: Why is it helpful to start a big project early?
quests.correctAnswer: You have time to fix problems 🔧
options: The project becomes shorter 📄
Nobody else can see your work 🙈
You have time to fix problems 🔧
quests.hint: Think about what could go wrong.
quests.explanation: Starting early gives you time to fix mistakes or ask for help.
quests.funFact: Projects often take longer than people expect.

quests.instruction: Which job comes first when you start a poster project?
quests.correctAnswer: Choose a topic and gather facts 🔍
options: Choose a topic and gather facts 🔍
Add the final decorations and borders ✨
Hand it in to your teacher to be marked 📥
quests.explanation: Knowing your topic and facts lets you design the poster properly.
quests.funFact: Writing a list of questions can help guide your research.

quests.instruction: Your teacher says tomorrow's project needs a notebook, a pencil, and a ruler. Which group should you prepare?
quests.correctAnswer: Notebook, pencil, ruler 🎒
options: Notebook, crayons, ruler 🎒
Notebook, pencil, glue 🎒
Notebook, pencil, ruler 🎒
quests.explanation: Listening to the exact list and matching it helps you arrive prepared.
quests.funFact: Writing down a list as the teacher says it helps you remember.

quests.instruction: Before you start an art project, what should you do first?
quests.correctAnswer: Gather all the supplies you need 📦
options: Gather all the supplies you need 📦
Begin and look for items as you go 🏃
Ask a friend to find them 🧑‍🤝‍🧑
quests.explanation: Having everything ready means you won't have to stop in the middle of your work.
quests.funFact: Many artists lay out their tools before beginning.

quests.instruction: You need to cut a straight strip of paper exactly 5 cm wide. Which two tools do you use together?
quests.correctAnswer: Ruler and scissors ✂️
options: Glue stick and stapler 🧴
Ruler and scissors ✂️
Eraser and sharpener ✏️
quests.explanation: The ruler shows the width, and scissors cut along it.
quests.funFact: Measure twice and cut once is a good saying.

quests.instruction: How can you stop your jumper from getting lost?
quests.correctAnswer: Write your name on it 🏷️
options: Leave it in the playground 🛝
Hide it in your bag 🎒
Write your name on it 🏷️
quests.explanation: A name label helps lost items find their owner.
quests.funFact: Labels can be sewn in or written with a marker.

quests.instruction: You can't find your jumper. What is a good first step?
quests.correctAnswer: Think where you last had it 🔍
options: Think where you last had it 🔍
Borrow a classmate's jumper for now 🧥
Decide it is lost and stop looking 😢
quests.hint: Your memory can point you to the right place to look.
quests.explanation: Remembering where you last wore it often leads you straight to it.
quests.funFact: Lost property boxes are a good second place to check.

quests.instruction: Where should small tools like erasers and sharpeners always go after use?
quests.correctAnswer: Back in your pencil case 👝
options: On the corner of your desk 🗄️
In your pocket until you need them 👖
Back in your pencil case 👝
quests.hint: Small things need a fixed home.
quests.explanation: Putting tools in the same place each time means you always know where they are.
quests.funFact: Pilots keep important items in the same place every time so they can find them without looking.

quests.instruction: You must read a 60-page book in 4 days. About how many pages is that each day?
quests.correctAnswer: 15 pages 📖
options: 10 pages 📖
15 pages 📖
30 pages 📖
quests.hint: Divide the pages by the days.
quests.explanation: 60 pages divided by 4 days is 15 pages each day.
quests.funFact: The division sign ÷ is called an obelus.

quests.instruction: Where should you keep a library book at home so you don't forget to return it?
quests.correctAnswer: In your school bag 🎒
options: In your school bag 🎒
Under your bed 🛏️
On a high shelf 📚
quests.hint: Keep it where you'll see it.
quests.explanation: Placing it with your school things makes it more likely to get back on time.
quests.funFact: Libraries often let you borrow books for two to three weeks.

quests.instruction: A library book is due Friday. When should you check that it's packed?
quests.correctAnswer: Thursday evening 🌙
options: Friday after school 🏠
Next week 🗓️
Thursday evening 🌙
quests.explanation: Checking the night before leaves time to find it if it's missing.
quests.funFact: Libraries often send reminders before books are due.

quests.instruction: School starts at 8:30 and the trip takes 20 minutes. When must you leave to arrive on time?
quests.hint: Count back from the start time.
quests.explanation: Counting back 20 minutes from 8:30 gives 8:10. Leaving a few minutes early is even safer.
quests.funFact: Clocks with hands are called analog clocks.

quests.instruction: Homework takes about 30 minutes. If you start at 5:00, when will you probably finish?
quests.explanation: 30 minutes after 5:00 is 5:30.
quests.funFact: There are 1,440 minutes in a day.

quests.instruction: A 40-minute lesson has gone on for 25 minutes. How long is left?
quests.correctAnswer: 15 minutes ⏱️
options: 25 minutes ⏱️
15 minutes ⏱️
10 minutes ⏱️
quests.explanation: 40 minus 25 leaves 15 minutes.
quests.funFact: The second hand takes 60 seconds to go once around the clock.

quests.instruction: Which question helps you check whether you really understand a topic?
quests.correctAnswer: Can I explain it to someone else? 🗣️
options: Did I read it through one time? 👀
Is my bag packed for tomorrow? 🎒
Can I explain it to someone else? 🗣️
quests.explanation: If you can explain it clearly, it's a good sign you understand it.
quests.funFact: Explaining ideas aloud is a great study method.

quests.instruction: After revising, you are still unsure about one part. What is a good next step?
quests.correctAnswer: Ask your teacher about that part 🙋
options: Ask your teacher about that part 🙋
Revise a different topic 📚
Ignore it and hope it won't come up 🤞
quests.explanation: Asking about the exact part you don't understand is the quickest way to fix it.
quests.funFact: Pinpointing what's unclear makes help more useful.

quests.instruction: Which is a clear, useful goal for studying?
quests.correctAnswer: Read for 10 minutes every evening 📖
options: Be the cleverest student in the class 🏆
Read for 10 minutes every evening 📖
Never make a single mistake again 🚫
quests.hint: A good goal is specific and doable.
quests.explanation: Specific goals are easier to follow and check than big, vague ones.
quests.funFact: Athletes and musicians often use small, clear goals to improve.

quests.instruction: You want to find the page about 'weather' in your textbook. Where do you look first?
quests.correctAnswer: The contents or index 📑
options: The first picture 🖼️
The back cover 📕
The contents or index 📑
quests.hint: Books list topics in a special place.
quests.explanation: The contents page lists chapters, and the index lists topics and their pages.
quests.funFact: An index is arranged in alphabetical order.

quests.instruction: In a dictionary, which word comes first: 'bat', 'ant', or 'cat'?
quests.correctAnswer: Ant 🐜
options: Ant 🐜
Cat 🐈
Bat 🦇
quests.explanation: Words are listed alphabetically, and 'a' comes before 'b' and 'c'.
quests.funFact: Dictionaries have guide words at the top of each page.

quests.instruction: Which part of a book explains the meaning of key words used in it?
quests.correctAnswer: Glossary 📘
options: Glossary 📘
Cover 📕
Title page 📄
quests.explanation: A glossary is a mini-dictionary for special words in that book.
quests.funFact: Science and history books often include a glossary.

quests.instruction: You save your science project on the school computer. Which is the best file name?
quests.correctAnswer: Science project - plants 💻
options: my stuff 💻
Science project - plants 💻
New Document 1 💻
quests.hint: A name should explain what is inside.
quests.explanation: A clear name tells you what the file is when you look for it later.
quests.funFact: Adding the date to a file name can help you find the newest version.

quests.instruction: Where should you store your files on a shared computer so you can find them again?
quests.correctAnswer: In a folder with your name or class 📁
options: In a folder with your name or class 📁
On the desktop with every other file 🖥️
Anywhere at all 🤷
quests.explanation: A folder with a clear name keeps your files together and separate from other people's.
quests.funFact: Folders can hold other folders, like a filing cabinet.

quests.instruction: You've finished on a shared computer. What should you do before you leave?
quests.correctAnswer: Save your work and log out 🔒
options: Turn off the screen only 🖥️
Save your work and log out 🔒
Leave it open for the next person 🔓
quests.explanation: Logging out keeps your work private so that others can't see or change it.
quests.funFact: Never share your password with anyone but a trusted adult.

quests.instruction: Two students at a table share one glue stick. How can they keep it organized?
quests.correctAnswer: Put it back in the middle each time 🧴
options: Keep it in your own bag until the project ends 🎒
Put it back in the middle each time 🧴
Pass it to whoever asks the loudest 📢
quests.hint: Make it easy for both to reach.
quests.explanation: Putting it back in a shared spot lets everyone find it.
quests.funFact: Twisting a glue stick down and putting the cap on keeps it from drying out.

quests.instruction: What keeps a marker's ink from drying out?
quests.correctAnswer: Put the cap back on firmly 🖊️
options: Leave them uncapped so the ink can air 🔓
Keep them on a sunny windowsill ☀️
Put the cap back on firmly 🖊️
quests.explanation: A tight cap keeps air out so the ink stays wet.
quests.funFact: Many markers can last for years if kept capped.

quests.instruction: Your group is doing a project. How should you arrange the shared tools?
quests.correctAnswer: In the center where everyone can reach 🧰
options: In the center where everyone can reach 🧰
In one person's bag for safe keeping 🎒
Spread around the room in different places 🏫
quests.explanation: Placing tools in a shared spot saves time and avoids arguments.
quests.funFact: Toolboxes and cutlery drawers use dividers so each item has its own place.

quests.instruction: It's Sunday evening. Tomorrow has a Math test, Art, and PE. Which plan is best?
quests.correctAnswer: Revise math notes and pack apron and shoes 🎒
options: Watch TV tonight and pack tomorrow morning 📺
Pack every book you own just to be safe 🏠
Revise math notes and pack apron and shoes 🎒
quests.hint: Prepare for each part of the day.
quests.explanation: Preparing for each thing on the timetable ahead of time makes mornings calm.
quests.funFact: People who plan ahead often feel less stress.

quests.instruction: A messy bag costs you five minutes each day looking for things. Which change would save the most time?
quests.correctAnswer: A folder per subject, packed by timetable 📁
options: A folder per subject, packed by timetable 📁
A much bigger bag to hold everything you own 🎒
Fewer pencils in your pencil case ✏️
quests.hint: Fix the cause of the problem.
quests.explanation: Sorting by subject and packing by timetable means everything has a place.
quests.funFact: Five minutes a day adds up to many hours over a school year.

quests.instruction: You have math, science, and English homework. What is the smartest way to start?
quests.correctAnswer: Check due dates and do the soonest first 📔
options: Start with the one you like the least 😖
Check due dates and do the soonest first 📔
Do the easiest one and leave the rest 🍃
quests.explanation: Doing the soonest deadline first prevents missed work.
quests.funFact: Planning can turn a big pile of homework into small, doable steps.
